changelog: Replace C1 to implement the primary finding: add a narrow contradiction veto that ranks boundaries with near‑certain entailment contradiction lowest while restricting the veto to well‑formed left fragments.
Delete E4 to reduce prompt size and bring the prompt back under the budget (removes a large example that was inflating prompt length).
Paraphrased C2 to be shorter while preserving the judgement about head-final dependency; frees space and keeps the same guidance.

Inserted a new core principle after C3 that constrains no-internal-split handling: do not shift cuts earlier if that leaves the left fragment missing its predicate/auxiliary/necessary head; prefer later intact boundaries. This directly addresses the primary finding.

Inserted a new core principle after C4 describing what a good dense cut looks like for very short-latency settings: allow denser boundaries only when the right fragment is independently translatable and the left fragment passes a narrow contradiction check.
Replace E1–E4 with four measured labeled examples from short/medium latency bins to teach the model about safe dense cuts that preserve predicate/attachment and avoid near‑certain contradiction.
Swapped handcrafted examples for real measured cases (≤3/≤5/≤7/≤10 bins) so the scorer learns where denser, safe boundaries are useful and how the target ranks them.
Insert a narrow, conditional contradiction‑veto at the top: rank near‑certainly contradicted left fragments lowest, but apply the veto only to well‑formed left chunks to avoid overblocking.

After C3, add a rule constraining 'no internal split' handling: do not move cuts earlier if that leaves the left fragment missing its predicate/auxiliary or required noun head; prefer later intact boundaries.

After C4, add a rule describing when dense cuts are acceptable: permit denser boundaries for very short‑latency only when right fragments are independently translatable and the contradiction veto does not apply.

Replace all four handcrafted examples with four measured labeled examples (ja_jp_1640, ja_jp_1256, ja_jp_1310, ja_jp_594) so the scorer learns from real cases that show near‑certain contradiction, predicate/attachment needs, and safe dense cuts.
